summary.prose: Building s3 starts with the shared definitions and a strict, serialised github.json module inside the daemon, then the three daemon methods, then the bounded terminal setup path, and finally each client (terminal, VS Code, JetBrains) and a contract test that proves all three show the same rows. Existing behaviour of the lenient resolver and of the shared socket client is pinned by tests before it is touched, and the many client tests that break when the shared types grow are updated in the same task that breaks them.

testStrategyCoverage.lldStrategyItem: REPO_TRACKER_FIELDS has a unique key per row and a kind of local, status or policy on every row, every local key is a GithubEntry field, and there is one policy row for each team rule in the real TeamPolicy type (team mode, signoff stages, claims enforced, claim units, administrators, forced task issues)

the branchPattern validator accepts feature/{type}/{id}-{slug}, {id}, {id}-{slug}, release/v1.2 and a pattern of exactly 200 characters, and rejects each of these with invalid-value naming the rule that failed: {user}, {id (unmatched), id} (unmatched), {}, a literal brace that is not a placeholder, a space, a character such as ~ ^ : ? * [ or a backslash, the empty string, 201 characters, a leading slash, a trailing slash, two consecutive slashes, '..' and a '.lock' ending
the branchPattern grammar is read from the single REPO_TRACKER_FIELDS row, and a test copy of the table with one more placeholder changes what the validator accepts without any change to a client
buildSettingsCatalog still returns every existing field unchanged, adds repoFields, stays pure and never throws for an empty or garbage config
validateRepoSetting accepts and rejects values per row: type enum, owner and repo names, ghPath and ghHost with a newline

readRepoEntry refuses an unreadable file, invalid JSON, a non-object top level, default that is null or an array or a primitive, repos that is null, an array or a primitive, and an own entry that is null, an array or a primitive, naming the failing level, and accepts a missing file, default, repos and entry

resolveGithubConfig keeps returning none for the inputs the loader rejects: a missing file, an unreadable file, invalid JSON and a file whose top level is not an object; every existing resolveGithubConfig test case passes without edits after the split into loadGithubConfigFile and resolveGithubConfigFromFile

characterization of the lenient API: for a null own entry and for a null default, resolveGithubConfig and resolveGithubConfigFromFile give exactly the result or the same thrown TypeError that the code gives before the split (recorded from the pre-split behaviour), so the split adds neither a new throw nor a new swallow

buildRepoSettings reports values from the repo's own entry only, the resolved target with its source, and the policy rows, including claimUnits built from a real TeamPolicy value, from a PolicyResult for none, team and ok:false

the sign-in mapping turns every whoAmI outcome into a signin.state: ok to signed-in with the login, and missing-tool, missing-signin (including an empty login), unreachable and rejected each to their own state with the reason, and a thrown exception to rejected
mergeRepoEntryKeys changes only the named keys, keeps the default entry, other repos and unknown keys, removes a key for null, and is a no-op for null on an unset key

writeRepoEntryKeys queue: many concurrent calls for different keys of the same file all land (none is lost), run one at a time (an instrumented fs seam never sees two overlapping writes), and a failing call (injected write error) does not stop the queued calls after it
writeRepoEntryKeys returns write-failed with the operating-system message and leaves the file and the temporary file as they were when the temporary write fails or the rename fails

writeRepoEntryKeys verify step: with an injected hook that changes the file after the temp write, the verify detects a different size, mtime or hash, discards the temp file and merges again from the new content; after the bounded attempts it returns file-changed and writes nothing

planTrackerConfig returns already only for a structurally valid file whose entry is complete (type github, owner, repo, pushTasks true, commitArtifacts true), needs-write with the owner and name from the origin remote when it is not, and failed with today's detail text when there is no origin remote

planTrackerConfig returns failed with the strict reader's message, calls no daemon and writes nothing for: a null own entry while the default is complete, a null default, an own entry that is an array or a primitive, a non-object top level, default or repos, and invalid JSON; none of these throws

runTrackerSetup with a configOutcome reports that outcome verbatim for the config step and neither reads nor writes github.json; without it the config step behaves as today and the existing setup tests pass unchanged
rpc without opts behaves exactly as before for a normal reply, a connection error and a reply split across data events (the existing ipc-client tests pass unchanged)

rpc with opts.timeoutMs rejects with a timeout error when a fake socket accepts the connection and never replies, and rejects with a closed error when the fake socket ends or closes before a reply; in both cases the socket is destroyed and the timer is cleared, and a normal reply inside the deadline resolves and clears the timer

repo identity: repo.settings.get and repo.settings.set key the entry on the exact registered path string; a symlink path that is not itself registered returns repo-not-registered, and two registered paths (a symlink and its target) keep separate entries with different settings

repo.settings.get reads the signed-in login only through s1's adapter: with a fake gh recording its commands, it runs the signed-in-user read once when the type is github, runs no other port method and changes no tracker state, and runs no gh command when the type is none
repo.settings.get returns what repo.settings.set just wrote, and a write made outside the daemon is shown on the next get (ac13)

repo.settings.set refuses a policy row, a status row, an unknown key, an invalid value (including an invalid branchPattern) and an unregistered repo with the right code, and writes nothing in each case
two clients' repo.settings.set calls issued at the same time through the daemon socket both land their keys

repo.trackerConfig.ensure writes type, owner, repo, pushTasks and commitArtifacts in one write, returns changed false when the entry is already complete, and refuses an unregistered repo and an invalid owner or name

tracker setup through the terminal service: with a running test daemon the config step reports done with today's detail text and the file holds the entry; with the entry already complete in a valid file it reports already and makes no daemon call; with no daemon it reports failed saying the daemon owns the file, writes nothing, and the other steps still report

tracker setup through the terminal service against a daemon that accepts the socket and never replies, and against one that closes the connection without a reply: the config step is reported failed within the deadline, the socket is released, and the other steps still report

tracker setup through the terminal service with a malformed github.json (null own entry with a complete default, null default): the config step is failed with the strict reader's message and no daemon call is made

makeServices always injects the daemon config seam: trackerSetup passes configOutcome into runTrackerSetup in every branch, and a source search test fails if code outside the daemon and the tests calls runTrackerSetup without it
a file or directory that is not writable makes the write return write-failed with the operating-system message

repo.settings.get and repo.settings.set on a file whose repos entry is null, whose default is null, whose top level is a primitive, or that holds invalid JSON, return github-json-unreadable, never throw and never report 'no tracker', and leave the original bytes untouched
repo.settings.get makes one read of github.json: a test counts the reads and rewrites the file after the read, and the result still describes the version that was read
a repo with no own target resolves to its git remote in the payload, and a default entry's owner and repo are never reported as the target (ac12)
repo.settings.get leaves github.json and the authored policy file byte for byte unchanged
